venue: Camp Randall Field House, U. of Wisconsin
supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy set featuring killer It Hurts Me Too and monster Good Lovin′
ai_show_review.blurb: The show bursts with a ferocious It Hurts Me Too, a scorching Hard To Handle that rolls straight into an expansive Good Lovin′. Pigpen’s raw vocals and harmonica add grit, while Phil’s bass drives the jams. Soundboard recordings capture the band at a tight, electric peak.
ai_show_review.review: The Dead bring their A‑game to Camp Randall Field House on March 14, 1971, delivering a set that crackles from the first chord. Jerry’s guitar is “really on,” cutting through with perfect tone and propelling each song forward, while Phil peels walls of bass that lift the jams to mesmerizing heights. Pigpen commands the stage on It Hurts Me Too, his primal howl and harmonica bite adding a gritty edge that fuels the band’s momentum. A standout moment arrives when Hard To Handle erupts into a smoking jam, building seamlessly into an absolute monster Good Lovin′ that showcases the group’s tight interplay and unbridled energy. The second set keeps the fire alive with classic numbers like Casey Jones and Wharf Rat, and the encore‑closing Uncle John’s Band caps off a night that feels both solid and inspired. The Cole soundboard capture (gd71-03-14.sbd.cole.6115.sbeok.shnf) preserves every nuance – crisp vocals, clear instrument separation, and just enough raw edge to make you feel like you’re right in the field house.

best_recording.reason: Crisp soundboard mix with excellent vocal clarity that captures the high‑energy set and standout jams.

key_highlights: Killer It Hurts Me Too performance with raw Pigpen vocals.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is on fire all night, delivering crisp leads and driving the jams with perfect tone.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh lays down a wall‑peeling bass line that anchors the high‑energy improvisations.
band_performance.Bob: Pigpen provides primal vocals on It Hurts Me Too and adds a standout harmonica shout, injecting raw grit into the set.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann (Billy) lays down a solid drum foundation that keeps the band tightly locked in.
